is a stage finish for the fourth time in La Vuelta.
The winners in Lorca are Italy’s Umberto Drei (1950), Belgium’s Jean Ronsmans (1970), and the USA’s Tyler Farrar (2010). The latter got the better of Koldo Fernandez and Mark Cavendish to take his fourth Grand Tour stage win (the 5th and final would come at the end of La Vuelta, in Madrid). Philippe Gilbert was wearing La Roja, the new overall leader’s jersey introduced that year.
Lorca has hosted La Vuelta stage starts in 1950, 1970 and 2017. On the last occasion, the race headed to Calar Alto, where tomorrow’s stage finishes.In 2015, Xabier Mikel Azparren (ITT) and Ivan Cobo (road race) dominated Spain’s U17 national championships in Lorca.
Lorca also took part in Spain’s 2019 national championships, hosting the finish of the women’s race (won by Lourdes Oyarbide) and the men U23 (Carmelo Urbano).Lorca has also been visited by local events, notably the Vuelta a Murcia."],"id":61178,"title":"Cycling memories from Lorca","publicationAt":"2026-09-02T16:02:09+02:00","slug":"cycling-memories-from-lorca","locale":"en","highlight":false,"updatedBy":"bvittek","updatedAt":"2026-09-02T16:02:09+02:00","stage":11,"_id":"f5ac7a1b5c1999eaf7df23d52d9bc24e8de31f9a204ae6a91948c40227cc7c59","_bind":"publication_en-2026-11","_origin":"news-2026-11","_updatedAt":1788357729776,"_parent":"stage-2026:5ce1301eb449fd522d920af164173ce278c773c186f9c1b536afe7075df6ae40","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:cycling-memories-from-lorca","model":"news"},{"publicationAt":"2026-09-02T13:41:48+02:00","text":["Lorca is the hometown of Juan Zurano, the first rider from Murcia to win a stage of La Vuelta, in 1973. He turned 78 yesterday.
The most famous rider from Murcia is Alejandro Valverde, whose list of achievements includes the overall victory at La Vuelta 2006. He won 12 stages in the Spanish Grand Tour, stood seven times on the overall podium (a record) and won 4 times the points standings (a shared record).Valverde won the 2019 national champion title in Murcia. The race started in Los Alcazares (km 36.2 on today’s route).
Among the most notable riders from Murcia, José Joaquin Rojas is in La Vuelta 26 as a sports director for Movistar.
José Luis Faura (Burgos Burpellet BH) is the local rider today. He hails from Pliego, around 50 kilometres north of Lorca."],"title":"Local heroes","pinned":false,"id":60761,"year":2026,"stageType":"PLN","createdAt":"2026-09-02T13:41:48+02:00","createdBy":"bvittek","type":"liv","picto":"liv_story","highlight":false,"stage":11,"updatedBy":"bvittek","updatedAt":"2026-09-02T13:41:48+02:00","slug":"local-heroes-2","locale":"en","_id":"57a79bd7851c737010a9b48bf775a3412494ed3ef6b9de4c3067f3fcc3a40d02","_bind":"publication_en-2026-11","_origin":"news-2026-11","_updatedAt":1788349309092,"_parent":"stage-2026:5ce1301eb449fd522d920af164173ce278c773c186f9c1b536afe7075df6ae40","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:local-heroes-2","model":"news"},{"year":2026,"type":"liv","stage":11,"text":["José Luis Faura (Burgos Burpellet BH) is the local rider today, hailing from Pliego, around 50 kilometres north of Lorca: "I’m really pleased to be able to race here, in front of my home crowd and everyone who supports me, on familiar roads. Let’s hope we can make our presence felt a bit. It’s not a very tough route, to be honest. Ultimately, the 1,000-metre climb over 150 kilometres is mainly because we’re starting from the coast and, as they say, we’re heading slightly inland, gradually climbing, with the Santa pass about 30 kilometres from the finish. I think it’s clear today is a day for sprinters. [{"stageType":"PLN","year":2026,"picto":"liv_story","createdAt":"2026-09-02T16:02:09+02:00","type":"liv","createdBy":"bvittek","pinned":false,"text":["Lorca is a stage finish for the fourth time in La Vuelta.
The winners in Lorca are Italy’s Umberto Drei (1950), Belgium’s Jean Ronsmans (1970), and the USA’s Tyler Farrar (2010). The latter got the better of Koldo Fernandez and Mark Cavendish to take his fourth Grand Tour stage win (the 5th and final would come at the end of La Vuelta, in Madrid). Philippe Gilbert was wearing La Roja, the new overall leader’s jersey introduced that year.
Lorca has hosted La Vuelta stage starts in 1950, 1970 and 2017. On the last occasion, the race headed to Calar Alto, where tomorrow’s stage finishes.In 2015, Xabier Mikel Azparren (ITT) and Ivan Cobo (road race) dominated Spain’s U17 national championships in Lorca.
Lorca also took part in Spain’s 2019 national championships, hosting the finish of the women’s race (won by Lourdes Oyarbide) and the men U23 (Carmelo Urbano).Lorca has also been visited by local events, notably the Vuelta a Murcia."],"id":61178,"title":"Cycling memories from Lorca","publicationAt":"2026-09-02T16:02:09+02:00","slug":"cycling-memories-from-lorca","locale":"en","highlight":false,"updatedBy":"bvittek","updatedAt":"2026-09-02T16:02:09+02:00","stage":11,"_id":"f5ac7a1b5c1999eaf7df23d52d9bc24e8de31f9a204ae6a91948c40227cc7c59","_bind":"publication_en-2026-11","_origin":"news-2026-11","_updatedAt":1788357729776,"_parent":"stage-2026:5ce1301eb449fd522d920af164173ce278c773c186f9c1b536afe7075df6ae40","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:cycling-memories-from-lorca","model":"news"},{"publicationAt":"2026-09-02T13:41:48+02:00","text":["Lorca is the hometown of Juan Zurano, the first rider from Murcia to win a stage of La Vuelta, in 1973. He turned 78 yesterday.
The most famous rider from Murcia is Alejandro Valverde, whose list of achievements includes the overall victory at La Vuelta 2006. He won 12 stages in the Spanish Grand Tour, stood seven times on the overall podium (a record) and won 4 times the points standings (a shared record).Valverde won the 2019 national champion title in Murcia. The race started in Los Alcazares (km 36.2 on today’s route).

Breakaway rider Lennard Kämna won the stage and Sepp Kuss retained La Roja.
Cartagena is a classic venue of the Vuelta a Murcia, recently witnessing the victories of Alessandro Covi (2022) and Ben Turner (2023).

Philippe Gilbert was wearing La Roja, the new overall leader’s jersey introduced that year.
Lorca has hosted La Vuelta stage starts in 1950, 1970 and 2017. On the last occasion, the race headed to Calar Alto, where tomorrow’s stage finishes.In 2015, Xabier Mikel Azparren (ITT) and Ivan Cobo (road race) dominated Spain’s U17 national championships in Lorca.

\nLorca has hosted La Vuelta stage starts in 1950, 1970 and 2017. On the last occasion, the race headed to Calar Alto, where tomorrow’s stage finishes.In 2015, Xabier Mikel Azparren (ITT) and Ivan Cobo (road race) dominated Spain’s U17 national championships in Lorca.

\nLorca has hosted La Vuelta stage starts in 1950, 1970 and 2017. On the last occasion, the race headed to Calar Alto, where tomorrow’s stage finishes.In 2015, Xabier Mikel Azparren (ITT) and Ivan Cobo (road race) dominated Spain’s U17 national championships in Lorca.

Philippe Gilbert was wearing La Roja, the new overall leader’s jersey introduced that year.

\nLorca has hosted La Vuelta stage starts in 1950, 1970 and 2017. On the last occasion, the race headed to Calar Alto, where tomorrow’s stage finishes.In 2015, Xabier Mikel Azparren (ITT) and Ivan Cobo (road race) dominated Spain’s U17 national championships in Lorca.

Philippe Gilbert was wearing La Roja, the new overall leader’s jersey introduced that year.
\nLorca has hosted La Vuelta stage starts in 1950, 1970 and 2017. On the last occasion, the race headed to Calar Alto, where tomorrow’s stage finishes.In 2015, Xabier Mikel Azparren (ITT) and Ivan Cobo (road race) dominated Spain’s U17 national championships in Lorca.
